name: Contract Bridge
description: Contract Bridge is the world's premier trick-taking card game, demanding extreme levels of logic, partnership cooperation, and psychological depth. Played by four players in two fixed partnerships, it consists of a complex auction (bidding) phase to determine the trump suit and trick goal, followed by the play of the hand where one player's cards (the dummy) are revealed. It is a game of intellectual mastery with a standardized global competitive circuit.

history.origins: Bridge evolved from 16th-century Whist via Auction Bridge. Contract Bridge was revolutionized by Harold S. Vanderbilt in 1925 who introduced the scoring system that rewards only tricks actually bid and made, adding a new layer of mathematical precision to the game.
timeline: 1890s: Bridge Whist replaces standard Whist in London card clubs.
1904: Auction Bridge emerges as the standard bidding variant.
1925: Harold Vanderbilt formalizes Contract Bridge scoring on a steamship cruise.
1930s: International matches popularize the game as a global intellectual sport.
Present: Governed by the World Bridge Federation (WBF) with Olympic observed status.
history.cultural: A symbol of peak mental skill, famously played by world leaders, scientists, and business icons. It is one of the few card games recognized as a competitive sport globally.
history.evolution: The decisive shift to Contract Bridge scoring made the auction as important as the card play, necessitating the development of elaborate bidding 'conventions' and partnership signals.

setup.players: 4 players. Partners sit opposite each other (North-South vs East-West).
setup.deck: Standard 52-card French pack (No Jokers). Suit rankings for bidding: No Trump > Spades > Hearts > Diamonds > Clubs.
setup.dealing: The entire deck is dealt out clockwise: 13 cards per player.
setup.equipment: Standard pack, bidding boxes, score pad.

rules.objective: Fulfill the trick count specified in the contract or prevent opponents from fulfilling theirs to score points.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Auction**: Players bid for the contract. 2. **Opening Lead**: Player to the left of the declarer plays the first card. 3. **Dummy**: Declarer's partner (the Dummy) lays their hand face-up on the table. 4. **Tricks**: 13 tricks are played. Must follow suit. Highest trump or highest led card wins.
keyRules: Only tricks bid and made score 'below the line' towards winning a game.
Vulnerability: Teams that have won one game become 'Vulnerable', increasing both bonuses and penalties.
Double/Redouble: Bids that increase the scoring stakes if the contract is made or broken.

strategy.basic: High Card Points (HCP): Ace=4, King=3, Queen=2, Jack=1. A partnership usually needs 25+ HCP to bid a game contract (4♥, 4♠, 3NT, etc.).
strategy.intermediate: Finessing: Win a trick with a lower card by predicting the location of a missing higher card in the opponent's hand. Communication: Use bidding levels to signal your card count and suit distribution to your partner.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Signaling: Use card play order (e.g., High-Low echo) to signal suit preference or card counts to your partner while defending. Squeezes: Force an opponent into a discard that unguards a master card.
tips: Trust your partner's bidding conventions—bridge is a game of information sharing.
Learn standard opening bids like 1NT (15-17 HCP) to simplify the auction.

variations.name: Duplicate Bridge
variations.description: The standard competitive format where the same hands are played at multiple tables to eliminate the luck of the deal.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Scoring table and vulnerability patterns differ but share the same base bidding and trick-play engine.

variations.name: Rubber Bridge
variations.description: The traditional home format where play continues until one side wins two games (the Rubber).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rubber format changes how games and rubbers are tallied while leaving core deal, auction, and play unchanged.

scoring.description: Complex scoring based on tricks bid and made (Below the Line) and overtricks/bonuses (Above the Line).
scoring.winCondition: Win two games (a Rubber) to win the match.

synthesis.shortDescription: Experience the world's most sophisticated trick-taking game. Communicate with your partner through a refined bidding auction, then execute a precise plan as you play 13 tricks with the 'Dummy' hand revealed. Contract Bridge is a masterclass in logic, memory, and strategy.
